# Analysis Pathways for 3-Phase Photon Representation

This document shows two analysis paths:
1. **Phasor (Sequence) Domain**: Abstract QM analysis
2. **Time Domain**: Physical measurement simulation

    Phasor1 --> Phasor2["<b>Convert to 3-Phase</b><br/>Inverse Fortescue<br/>(I<sub>a</sub>, I<sub>b</sub>, I<sub>c</sub>) = F<sup>-1</sup>(I<sub>0</sub>, I<sub>1</sub>, I<sub>2</sub>)<br/>Complex amplitudes"]

## Key Differences Between Paths

### Phasor Domain (Left Path)
- **Input**: Complex amplitudes (I₁, I₂)
- **Analysis**: Matrix algebra, eigenvalues
- **Measurement**: Instantaneous projection
- **Output**: Quantum correlation function
- **Shows**: Spin structure, entanglement

### Time Domain (Right Path)
- **Input**: Oscillating signals I_a(t), I_b(t), I_c(t)
- **Analysis**: PLL synchronization, Park transform
- **Measurement**: Physical process (sync + rotate + average)
- **Output**: Time-averaged correlation
- **Shows**: Physical mechanism, energy flow

### Both Paths Give Same Result
**E(θ_A, θ_B) = -cos(θ_A - θ_B)**

Bell violations: **S = 2√2 > 2**

# Comparison Table

| Aspect | Phasor Domain | Time Domain |
|--------|---------------|-------------|
| **Input** | Complex amplitudes (I₁, I₂) | Oscillating signals I_a(t), I_b(t), I_c(t) |
| **Transform** | Fortescue (eigendecomp) | PLL + Park (rotation) |
| **Time** | No time evolution | Explicit time dependence |
| **Measurement** | Matrix projection | Physical process (integration) |
| **Output** | Quantum correlation | Time-averaged correlation |
| **Shows** | WHAT (spin states) | HOW (measurement mechanism) |
| **Result** | E(θ,φ) = -cos(θ-φ) | E(θ,φ) = -cos(θ-φ) ✓ |

Both paths are **mathematically equivalent** but provide different insights!

# Mathematical Objects Summary

## Phasor Domain

**State vector:**
$$|\psi\rangle = \begin{pmatrix} \alpha \\ \beta \end{pmatrix}, \quad |\alpha|^2 + |\beta|^2 = 1$$

**Fortescue operator:**
$$F = \frac{1}{3}\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & \alpha & \alpha^2 \\ 1 & \alpha^2 & \alpha \end{pmatrix}, \quad \alpha = e^{j2\pi/3}$$

**Sequences:**
$$\begin{pmatrix} I_0 \\ I_1 \\ I_2 \end{pmatrix} = F \begin{pmatrix} I_a \\ I_b \\ I_c \end{pmatrix}$$

## Time Domain

**Phase currents:**
$$I_a(t) = \text{Re}[I_1 e^{j\omega t} + I_2 e^{-j\omega t}]$$

**Park transform:**
$$\begin{pmatrix} I_d \\ I_q \\ I_0 \end{pmatrix} = P(\theta) \begin{pmatrix} I_a \\ I_b \\ I_c \end{pmatrix}$$

where:
$$P(\theta) = \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\begin{pmatrix} 
\cos\theta & \cos(\theta-120°) & \cos(\theta-240°) \\
-\sin\theta & -\sin(\theta-120°) & -\sin(\theta-240°) \\
1/\sqrt{2} & 1/\sqrt{2} & 1/\sqrt{2}
\end{pmatrix}$$

## Both Give Same Correlation

$$E(\theta_A, \theta_B) = -\cos(\theta_A - \theta_B)$$

$$S_{\text{CHSH}} = 2\sqrt{2} \approx 2.828 > 2$$
